audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit structurally required working-capital reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $62.563 million cumulative operating cash use in 2024-2025; 2025 inventory and receivables increased $29.028 million and $22.902 million, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: A normalized working-capital reinvestment charge would reduce forecast owner earnings and every scenario's operating present value.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used in operating activities was $9,137,000 during 2025 as compared to $53,426,000 during 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash absorption is demonstrated and is approximately four times the $15.7 million annual anchor. The record does not prove that all of it is permanent: first-half 2026 operating cash flow recovered to $44.144 million, largely through receivable collections, although inventory still increased $19.576 million. Even a modest recurring fraction would materially reduce value, so the possible omission is material despite the normalized amount remaining unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each historical OE year to operating cash flow, separate reversible backlog timing from permanent working-capital growth, estimate normalized working capital per dollar of Defense sales, and rerun all scenarios with that reinvestment charge.

audit_findings.title: The failed vendor deposit could be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.701 million, equal to 17.2% of the $15.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If both the impairment embedded in net income and the same deposit within capital expenditure were deducted, 2025 OE and potentially the trend-based anchor are understated.
audit_findings.evidence: The deposit had been carried in Property, Plant and Equipment on the Company’s balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $2.701 million deposit was impaired after being carried in PP&E, and consolidated 2025 PP&E purchases of $27.034 million exceed reported segment capital expenditures of $24.333 million by exactly $2.701 million. That establishes a double-counting pathway, but the supplied record does not show the detailed 2025 OE calculation and therefore does not demonstrate that the valuation actually used both deductions. Its effect on the ten-year log-trend anchor is also not established.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE calculation line by line; if it used consolidated PP&E purchases while retaining the impairment in earnings, remove one $2.701 million deduction, recompute the historical trend and anchor, and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator predates a material warehouse-perimeter change
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.510 million sale proceeds, $1.707 million gain, $2.359 million first-half 2026 startup costs, and $1.037 million first-half 2026 short-term and variable lease costs; normalized net effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The completed sale affects the cash bridge, while the new rent, transition costs, avoided ownership costs, and Nettleton maintenance requirements affect normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Canton facility was sold on February 10, 2026 and subsequently leased back under a short term lease agreement, as the Company transitions all warehousing functions to the Nettleton facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: FY2025 OE predates the Canton sale, while the July 2026 bridge follows it. The bridge may properly contain the sale proceeds, but FY2025 earnings do not represent the completed warehouse configuration. Known transition amounts are meaningful relative to the $15.7 million anchor, yet the permanent net effect is indeterminate because temporary startup costs, post-sale rent, avoided Canton costs, and Nettleton costs are not reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Build a pro forma annual OE for the completed Nettleton configuration, excluding the $1.707 million sale gain and temporary transition costs while including ongoing rent, avoided Canton ownership costs, and Nettleton maintenance capex; confirm that the $4.510 million proceeds are captured only once in the July bridge, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: Owned leased real estate needs coherent income and asset treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.351 million 2025 lease income, equal to 15.0% of the $15.7 million anchor; property-level net contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retained lease income raises OE only if related operating expenses and maintenance capex remain included; alternatively, removing the income requires separately adding the leased property's value to the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Lease income from operating lease payments was $ 2,351,000 , $ 2,283,000 , $ 2,281,000 for the years ended December 31, 2025 , 2024 , and 2023 , respectively and is included in Other income on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated method purges portfolio interest income, not all other income, so omission of lease income is not demonstrated. However, the detailed OE schedule does not establish whether lease income, property expenses, and maintenance capex were treated consistently. The gross income is large enough relative to the anchor to matter, but the direction and net magnitude cannot be determined without property-level costs.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $2.351 million lease income through OE and identify the associated taxes, insurance, utilities, depreciation adjustment, and maintenance capex. Either retain the complete net property cash flow in OE or remove it and add a separately supported property value, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: All reported cash may not be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $16.291 million, or $2.28 per share and 7.2% of the $225 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating cash should be excluded from the cash-and-short-term-investment bridge addition rather than added as surplus equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has sufficient liquidity in the form of cash and cash equivalents and marketable securities and credit facilities to meet all of its anticipated capital requirements, to make dividend payments, and to fund future growth through acquisitions and other means.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether all cash is surplus remains unresolved, particularly given inventory funding and the $38.116 million construction agreements. Nevertheless, even treating none of the $16.291 million as excess would reduce base value from $31.59 to approximately $29.31 per share. That maximum effect cannot change the conclusion relative to the $147.72 market price and is modest compared with the valuation gap.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating liquidity from seasonal cash lows, backlog production needs, supplier commitments, construction spending, and available credit; reduce the bridge by the supported amount in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: A legacy environmental claim may be absent from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum undiscounted liability of $0.925 million, or approximately $0.13 per share and 0.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If scheduled remediation payments are absent from forecast OE, their present value should be deducted as a non-debt claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s environmental accrued liability on an undiscounted basis was $ 925,000 as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 , and is included in accrued liabilities on its balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The $0.925 million obligation and payment schedule are filed facts, but the record does not establish whether forecast OE already captures the cash payments. Even complete omission would overstate the $225 million base equity value by no more than 0.4% before discounting, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged by a wide margin.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the environmental reserve at July 5, 2026 and trace the scheduled payments through forecast OE; if absent, deduct their present value from the bridge.
